answer: The pit master issues a ticket for every load of coal cut from the marked seam, and the loads are weighed at the pit head before they may be sold. A reef load hauled from another seam fails the ticket: at the ivory of the coal the grain must match the seam the ticket names, and a strange load burns wrong in the stove. Forging the tickets means bribing the pit master, faking a year of cutting records and paying 21,100, and the vertex ticket is kept in the station office, so a load whose ticket number repeats is seized at the gate.
